meta.title: Plan 6, re-planned: prove artefacto with real agents before loadout adopts it
meta.goal_md: Take artefacto from *green in its own suite* to *installed and driven by real agents*, and only then decide whether loadout switches over to it.
meta.summary_md: Everything artefacto's spec lists for v1 is built and on `main` except two things: no release has been cut, so the installer one-liner points at a URL that does not exist yet, and no real Claude Code or Codex session has ever run the skill. The loadout dispatcher (loadout PR #57) is built and green, but it assumes both. This plan puts the release and the agent tests first, keeps the loadout decision last, and treats the loop you are running right now, reviewing this plan on this page, as the first Claude Code test.
key_points: **Release first** (`p-release`): push the `v0.1.0` tag, let the workflow build the four archives and the installer, and install from it on this Mac.

**Claude Code is being tested as you read this** (`t-loop-claude`): this page was pushed from a Claude Code session following the skill as written. Comment, ask questions in a thread and at page level, tick things, send the review; the answers and the next revision are the evidence.
**Codex gets the same review with the poll loop** (`p-codex`), where the risks are different: a sandbox that forbids listening sockets, and command timeouts shorter than `await`'s 90 seconds.
**Loadout waits** (`p-loadout`): PR #57 stays open until both agent runs pass; merging or closing it is the last task, not the first.
out_of_scope: Question `options` (spec 12 defers it; answers stay free text)
Real screenshots as posters (drawn posters stay)

phases.title: Make it installable
phases.summary_md: The cargo-dist configuration is on `main` and `dist plan` lists what a tag would build; nothing has been built. Until the tag is pushed, every install instruction, including loadout's offer, is a promise.

tasks.title: Cut v0.1.0
tasks.summary_md: Push the `v0.1.0` tag. The release workflow builds `artefacto-x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `artefacto-installer.sh`, checksums, and the source tarball, and publishes a GitHub release. This is a public release; the tag is pushed only when you say so (`q-release`).

files.note: already committed; nothing to change unless the workflow fails
generated by dist; fix only if a build fails

acceptance: `gh release view v0.1.0` lists four archives, `artefacto-installer.sh`, and `sha256.sum`
the workflow's four build jobs are green

tasks.title: Install from the release on this Mac
tasks.summary_md: Run the one-liner artefacto documents, `curl -LsSf …/artefacto-installer.sh | sh`, on this machine. It should land in `~/.cargo/bin`, write the receipt cargo-dist installers write, and answer `artefacto --version` with `0.1.0`. This is also what loadout's install offer would run.
acceptance: `artefacto --version` prints `artefacto 0.1.0` from `~/.cargo/bin`
`~/.config/artefacto/artefacto-receipt.json` exists
`artefacto plan push` of a fixture opens a page from the installed binary, not a build

tasks.title: Install the skill by agent name, not by directory
tasks.summary_md: The installer only installs the binary; cargo-dist's `curl | sh` script has no step where it could ask which agents you use. Choosing agents happens one command later. Today that command takes a directory (`artefacto skill --install ~/.claude/skills`). Add `--for claude`, `--for codex`, and `--for all`, each resolving to the directory that agent reads (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.codex/skills`), with `--install DIR` kept for anything else. The README's install section shows the `--for` line.
acceptance: `artefacto skill --for claude,codex` writes both packages and prints the paths
an unknown agent name lists the known ones and exits 2

tasks.title: Install on Linux
tasks.summary_md: The same one-liner in a Linux container or box, to see the Linux archive and the daemon's `fork`/`flock` paths work off this Mac. Optional; `q-linux` asks whether it is worth doing now.
acceptance: `artefacto plan push` and `artefacto await` work in a Linux shell

tasks.title: README says how to install and how to start
tasks.summary_md: The README's Status paragraph still says only the static renderer works. Replace it with what exists: install (the one-liner, or `cargo install --path .`), one skill line per agent (`artefacto skill --for claude,codex` once `t-skill-targets` lands; the directory form until then), and the five-line loop.
acceptance: a reader can install artefacto and its skill from the README alone

phases.title: Prove the loop in Claude Code
phases.summary_md: The skill's Claude Code section names tools (a Monitor on the follow line, `ack` per frame, `PushNotification`, `TaskStop`) that no test runs. The proof is a real session following the skill with a real reviewer. That session is this one.

tasks.title: Install the skill for Claude Code
tasks.summary_md: `artefacto skill --install ~/.claude/skills` puts `artefacto-plan/SKILL.md` and `reference.md` where Claude Code reads skills. Then a fresh Claude Code session should list the skill and pick it up from its description when asked to show a plan visually.
acceptance: `~/.claude/skills/artefacto-plan/SKILL.md` exists with the frontmatter Claude Code requires
a fresh session invokes the skill when asked to review a plan

tasks.title: Run a real review from Claude Code, with you as the reviewer
tasks.summary_md: This plan is the run. It was written as `plan.json`, checked, and pushed by this session; a Monitor is armed on the follow line. What the reviewer does next is the test: comment on a task, ask a question inside a thread, ask one at page level, tick a few elements, answer an open question, send the review with *request changes*, then approve the next revision. The agent must answer each chat where it was asked, push one revision carrying every resolution, and stop when approved, without improvising anything the skill does not say.
acceptance: every chat message got a reply in the thread it was asked in, and none twice
the sent review produced exactly one revision with every comment resolved as changed or declined, each with a note
`reviewer.idle` produced one banner, `reviewer.away` one notification
the monitor was stopped when the review was approved
`artefacto status --json` ends with the artifact at revision ≥ 2 and 0 open threads

tasks.title: Record what the run found, and fix it
tasks.summary_md: Anything the agent got wrong, anything the skill left unclear, anything the page or server did that surprised the reviewer. Skill prose fixes go into `skills/artefacto-plan/`; product defects get a test first; the record goes into `docs/BUILD-STATUS.md` under *What the first real use found*.
acceptance: every finding is either fixed with a test or recorded with a reason

phases.title: Prove the loop in Codex
phases.summary_md: Codex has no monitor, so it runs the skill's generic section: push, then `artefacto await` every 90 seconds, acting on each result and acknowledging it on the next call. Two things could break that before the loop even starts.

tasks.title: Install the skill for Codex
tasks.summary_md: `artefacto skill --install ~/.codex/skills`. Codex reads project and user skills in the same `SKILL.md` format; confirm a session lists it.
acceptance: a Codex session lists `artefacto-plan` and invokes it when asked to review a plan

tasks.title: Run the same review from Codex with the poll loop
tasks.summary_md: The same script as `t-loop-claude`, driven by `artefacto await --session … --ack <seq>` calls. Watch for the two known hazards: if Codex's sandbox forbids listening sockets, `push` cannot start the daemon and the skill's fallback applies (`artefacto serve --foreground` in your own terminal, or `artefacto plan render` for a static page and the paste-back flow); if Codex kills a command before 90 seconds, `await --timeout 60s` is the fix and the skill should say so.
acceptance: the same five outcomes as `t-loop-claude`, through `await` instead of a monitor
an expired lease (five quiet minutes) is recovered the way the skill says: `await` without `--session` under the same name

tasks.title: Record what Codex found, and fix it
tasks.summary_md: As `t-claude-findings`, for the poll loop and the generic section of the skill. If the sandbox hazard is real, the skill's opening should say when to use `render` instead of `push`.
acceptance: every finding is either fixed with a test or recorded with a reason

phases.title: Close out v1
phases.summary_md: What the spec lists that is not built, and the low notes the last review left. Small, and cheaper to do before any agent depends on the answers.

tasks.title: Make asking the agent obvious on every element
tasks.summary_md:
Found in this run. Today *Ask the agent* is offered in two places only: the bottom bar, and inside a thread after a comment exists. There is no way to ask about a task or a risk without commenting on it first, and inside a thread *Reply* and *Ask the agent* look alike although only Ask wakes the agent. Three changes: an Ask control wherever Comment is offered (the element toolbar on tasks, phases, risks, and open questions), Ask styled as the primary action with an icon so it reads differently from Reply, and one hint line in the bar the first time the page opens: *comments wait for your review; questions reach the agent now*.

Built as artefacto PR #8: one actions row per element, the ask outlined in the accent, one `chat.sent` that opens the thread, `asked` wherever threads are listed, the banner corrected, the hint in the bar, and a question composer that says who hears it. Reviewed fresh (round eighteen), 19 mutations caught, 514 tests green.

`chat.send` with a `ref` and no thread opens the thread and asks in one command
ask from a task with no comment; screenshot

acceptance: every element that offers Comment also offers Ask the agent
asking on an element with no thread creates the thread and delivers `chat.sent` with `data.thread` set

tasks.title: Build `--passive live`, or cut it
tasks.summary_md: `serve --passive live` parses today and does nothing. The spec's rule: at most one passive frame per 30 seconds, a five-minute age cap, and repeated edits to one element coalesced. Digest is the default and is what both agent runs use, so `q-live` asks whether v1 needs live at all; if not, the flag goes and the spec says why.
acceptance: under a synthetic storm of edits, at most one passive frame per 30 seconds reaches the agent

tasks.title: The three low notes from the merge review
tasks.summary_md: The index page inlines a poster by the row id from `index.json` without validating it (a hand-edited `../x` would read an arbitrary file into the page); `clean` has a window between stopping the server and taking the startup lock; the release workflow runs its plan job on every pull request. Each is a few lines and a test.
acceptance: a row id the mint would refuse is skipped on the index page
`clean` re-checks for a live server after taking the lock

phases.title: Then, and only then, loadout
phases.summary_md: Loadout PR #57 is built, green, and reviewed twice. It stays open until the two agent runs pass. If artefacto changed on the way, loadout's `TESTED_VERSION` and the plan skill it reads follow. Whether it merges at all is `q-loadout`.

tasks.title: Install artefacto in loadout's CI
tasks.summary_md: Loadout's two real-binary tests skip without `LOADOUT_ARTEFACTO_REAL`. Once the release exists, the CI job can install artefacto with the one-liner and set the variable, so the dispatcher is tested against the real binary on every loadout PR.
acceptance: loadout's `test` job runs `plan_render_and_check_with_the_real_artefacto` rather than skipping it

tasks.title: Decide loadout PR #57
tasks.summary_md: With both agent runs passed and their findings fixed: bump loadout's `TESTED_VERSION` if artefacto moved, then a fresh review-and-merge as for the artefacto PRs, or close the PR if loadout should keep its own plan module for now.
acceptance: PR #57 is merged or closed, and the reason is in its thread

risks.title: The installer URL does not exist until the tag is pushed
risks.mitigation_md: `t-tag` comes first. Until then, install with `cargo install --path ~/_git/artefacto`; loadout's install offer would fail with a 404 today.

risks.title: An agent sandbox may forbid listening sockets
risks.mitigation_md: The daemon binds a loopback port. Where that is refused, the skill's fallback is `artefacto serve --foreground` in the user's own terminal, or `artefacto plan render` for a static page with the paste-back flow. `t-loop-codex` finds out which.

risks.title: The Claude Code section names tools no test has run
risks.mitigation_md: `t-loop-claude` is exactly that test, in this session, with the Monitor armed on the follow line.

risks.title: A harness may kill a command before 90 seconds
risks.mitigation_md: `await --timeout 60s` (or shorter); the skill can say so once a harness is known to need it.

risks.title: `open` from an agent process may not reach the browser
risks.mitigation_md: The one-time URL is always printed; `artefacto open` mints a fresh one.

open_questions.question_md: Push the `v0.1.0` tag now and make the release public? Everything in `p-release` and the loadout CI task waits on it.
Test the Linux archive now (a container is enough), or Mac only until someone needs Linux?
Does v1 need `--passive live`, or should the flag go until a real reviewer asks for every interaction as it happens?
Once both agent runs pass, does loadout switch over (merge PR #57), or keep its own plan module for now?

Which agents should `skill --for` know at v0.1.0? Claude Code and Codex are the two being tested. Gemini, opencode, and cursor-agent are installed here too, but their skill directories are unconfirmed.
